title: A Microscopic View of Protein Soft and Reactive Landing on Flexible Polyethylene Glycol Surfaces.
one_liner_zh: 该文用ReaxFF反应力场模拟蛋白质与PEG表面的碰撞沉积过程，虽以蛋白质为对象并涉及结构保持，但核心是表面沉积动力学而非蛋白质结构计算建模，方法可迁移性有限。
abstract: The interaction of proteins with polymer surfaces is central to understanding biomaterial compatibility and developing advanced deposition techniques. In this work, we investigate the collision dynamics of lysozyme and neurotensin with polyethylene glycol (PEG) surfaces in the vacuum using the reactive force field (ReaxFF). These simulations mimic the soft and reactive landing processes encountered in electrospray ionization (ESI)-, matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization (MALDI)- and cluster ion beam-based preparative mass spectrometry approaches. Various PEG structures, including vertically aligned chains and amorphous configurations, with or without surface chain terminations, were considered. Collision velocities ranging from 1 to 6 km/s were employed to explore structural preservation, energy transfer, and chemical bond formation between the biomolecules and the PEG. For lysozyme ( approximately 14 kDa), where 1 km/s corresponds to approximately 74 eV, our results show that PEG acts as a soft, cushion-like substrate, effectively dissipating impact energy and preserving protein structure under most conditions. Notably, covalent bond formation was observed only at high velocity (>/=5 km/s) in the amorphous PEG structure lacking surface chain terminations. The findings indicate that PEG offers a promising medium for preserving protein integrity during deposition, maintaining the capacity to build protein multilayers, and potentially facilitating controlled protein desorption in solvents when desired. Even though defining an exact energy threshold would require a more detailed investigation, our simulations also constitute a proof-of-principle that the molecular fragments also transferred in iBEAM may act as mediators to induce protein grafting at relatively low velocity (3 km/s).
abstract_zh: 蛋白质与聚合物表面的相互作用是理解生物材料相容性及开发先进沉积技术的核心。在本研究中，我们利用反应力场（Reactive Force Field, ReaxFF）在真空条件下探讨了溶菌酶和神经降压素与聚乙二醇（polyethylene glycol, PEG）表面的碰撞动力学。这些模拟模仿了电喷雾电离（ESI）、基质辅助激光解吸/电离（MALDI）及团簇离子束基制备性质谱方法中遇到的软着陆和反应性着陆过程。我们考虑了多种PEG结构，包括垂直排列链和无定形构型，并设有或无表面链终止的情况。采用1至6 km/s的碰撞速度，以探索生物分子与PEG之间的结构保持、能量转移及化学键形成。对于溶菌酶（约14 kDa），其中1 km/s对应约74 eV，我们的结果表明，PEG作为一种柔软的缓冲型基底，能有效耗散冲击能量，并在大多数条件下保持蛋白质结构。值得注意的是，仅在无表面链终止的无定形PEG结构中，且速度不低于5 km/s时，观察到共价键形成。研究结果表明，PEG为沉积过程中保持蛋白质完整性提供了有前景的介质，同时维持构建蛋白质多层的能力，并在需要时可能促进溶剂中蛋白质的可控解吸。尽管确定精确的能量阈值需要更详细的研究，我们的模拟也构成了一项原理验证，即iBEAM中转移的分子碎片可能作为介体，在相对较低速度（3 km/s）下诱导蛋白质接枝。
